title: Futures foretold (Kern ch. 6)
hookLine: the great disciples are told their future Buddha names and lands
tomorrow: The long story of a past Buddha (Kern ch. 7)

lines: NAMES READ ONE AT A TIME.
IS MY NAME ON THE LIST?
cards: At a graduation, the names are read out one at a time. Each person waits for theirs. Some are calm.
Some are gripping the arm of the chair. And between one name and the next, the people still waiting wonder if theirs is really on the list.
Chapter six of the Lotus has that moment in it, except the list is of future Buddhas, and the ones waiting are some of the Buddha's closest disciples.

teach.b: Vyakarana is the Sanskrit word the Lotus uses for this kind of announcement: a prediction, a declaration, the Buddha saying out loud what someone's future will be. Sariputra received one in chapter three.
Chapter six is named for it.
The Buddha turns to Mahakasyapa, one of the disciples who told the story of the lost son, and declares that after honoring many Buddhas in ages to come, he will become a Buddha himself.

Kern gives the name as Rasmiprabhasa, and the sutra describes his land: level, clean, with jeweled trees, free of rubble and thorns. Now the other great disciples, Subhuti, Katyayana and Maudgalyayana, are trembling.
In Kern's translation they speak to the Buddha in verse, with a picture worth keeping.

teach.h: A STARVING MAN AT A ROYAL MEAL.
teach.b: We are like a man who has come out of a famine, they say, and finds a royal meal set in front of him. He is starving, but he doesn't dare touch it until the king himself says: eat.
They have heard that disciples can become Buddhas. They can't quite believe it applies to them until the Buddha says so by name. And the Buddha does.

One by one he declares each a future Buddha, gives each a Buddha name, and describes each one's land and how long their teaching will last. The sutra takes its time over every one, as if no one should be hurried past.
That is vyakarana in the Lotus. Not a horoscope about Tuesday. A teacher looking at a student and saying, in front of everyone: I see where you are going, and I am sure of it.
The starving man is allowed to eat.

how: In Mahayana Buddhism a vyakarana is a Buddha's prediction that someone will reach Buddhahood; the Lotus Sutra gives a series of them, and some East Asian teachers read them as the one vehicle spoken to each hearer by name.

o: a reading of the stars to tell your fortune
a declaration of someone's future as a Buddha
a vow a monk makes on the day he is ordained

games.q: a future foretold: tap the pairs.
p: won't eat until the king says so

s: a vyakarana in the Lotus is like a daily horoscope
it is the Buddha's declaration that someone will become a Buddha, with a name and a land.
the waiting disciples compare themselves to a starving man at a royal meal
he dares not eat until the king himself tells him to.
in chapter six only Kasyapa receives a prediction
Subhuti, Katyayana and Maudgalyayana are each named too.

games.q: you've come out of a famine and a royal meal is set in front of you. you are starving. what do you do?
o: wait until the king says eat
take a little and hide it for later
games.why: the disciples say they are like that man: they won't believe the promise is for them until the Buddha says so. then he names each of them.

practice: Is there someone waiting, quietly, to be told they'll be all right: a friend between jobs, a teenager, someone recovering?
Silently wish them well about the road ahead, in a few plain words of your own, and hold the wish out the way you'd hold a meal out to someone hungry.

wordCard.voice: Vyakarana. A prediction or declaration: in the Lotus, the Buddha announcing that a disciple will become a Buddha, with a name and a land of their own. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a declaration or prediction; the title of chapter six in Kern's Sanskrit text.

carryVoice: Your line: a future foretold. Like the king's word to a hungry man: eat. I'll be here tomorrow.
